headline.title: ARMOR 2025: A Military-Aligned Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Beyond Civilian Contexts
headline.summary: The article introduces ARMOR 2025, a benchmark designed to assess the safety of large language models (LLMs) specifically in military contexts, addressing the need for evaluation methods that align with military operational standards. It highlights the potential of LLMs to improve decision-making and operational efficiency in defense applications while emphasizing the limitations of existing safety benchmarks that primarily focus on civilian risks.

articles.title: AirFM-DDA: Air-Interface Foundation Model in the Delay-Doppler-Angle Domain for AI-Native 6G
articles.summary: Researchers have introduced AirFM-DDA, a new air-interface foundation model designed for AI-native 6G networks, which operates in the Delay-Doppler-Angle domain to improve physical layer design. This model addresses limitations of existing approaches that rely on channel state information in the space-time-frequency domain, enhancing the learning of universal channel representations.

articles.title: Dynamic-TD3: A Novel Algorithm for UAV Path Planning with Dynamic Obstacle Trajectory Prediction
articles.summary: The article introduces Dynamic-TD3, a new algorithm designed for UAV path planning that incorporates dynamic obstacle trajectory prediction. This framework aims to address the safety-exploration dilemma in deep reinforcement learning by enforcing strict safety constraints while maintaining performance in the presence of sensor noise and intent uncertainty.

articles.title: NorBERTo: A ModernBERT Model Trained for Portuguese with 331 Billion Tokens Corpus
articles.summary: NorBERTo is a new encoder model based on the ModernBERT architecture, specifically designed for Portuguese and trained on a large corpus of 331 billion tokens from the Aurora-PT dataset. This model enhances Natural Language Processing capabilities in Portuguese by incorporating long-context support and efficient attention mechanisms.

articles.title: Odysseus: Scaling VLMs to 100+ Turn Decision-Making in Games via Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: The paper presents Odysseus, a method for scaling vision-language models (VLMs) to handle over 100 turns in decision-making tasks within video games using reinforcement learning. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods that depend on extensive supervised fine-tuning or are restricted to short-horizon settings.

articles.title: BWLA: Breaking the Barrier of W1AX Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
articles.summary: The article introduces BWLA, a novel approach to post-training quantization for large language models (LLMs) that aims to reduce memory and compute demands by binarizing weights to 1 bit. This method addresses the limitations of existing quantization techniques by effectively managing activation heavy tails, enabling true end-to-end acceleration in LLM deployment.

articles.title: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
articles.summary: A11y-Compressor is a proposed framework designed to improve the efficiency of AI agents' observations of graphical user interfaces by transforming linearized accessibility trees into more compact and structured representations. This approach aims to reduce redundancy and enhance the understanding of spatial relationships among UI elements, facilitating more reliable grounding for AI interactions.

articles.title: BlenderRAG: High-Fidelity 3D Object Generation via Retrieval-Augmented Code Synthesis
articles.summary: BlenderRAG is a new system designed to enhance the automatic generation of executable Blender code from natural language by utilizing a retrieval-augmented approach. It operates on a curated dataset of 500 expert-validated examples across 50 object categories, aiming to reduce syntactic errors and improve the geometric consistency of generated 3D objects.

articles.title: InpaintSLat: Inpainting Structured 3D Latents via Initial Noise Optimization
articles.summary: Researchers have introduced InpaintSLat, a training-free method for controllable 3D inpainting that leverages initial noise optimization within a structured 3D latent diffusion framework. The approach addresses stability issues in inpainting and editing tasks by capitalizing on the sensitivity of geometric structures established early in the diffusion process.

articles.title: A hybrid solution approach for the Integrated Healthcare Timetabling Competition 2024
articles.summary: Team Twente's submission for the Integrated Healthcare Timetabling Competition 2024 ranked third, utilizing a hybrid solution approach that integrates mixed-integer programming, constraint programming, and simulated annealing. The methodology involves a three-phase process that decomposes the problem into subproblems, with insights and design decisions detailed in the work.

articles.title: D3-Gym: Constructing Real-World Verifiable Environments for Data-Driven Discovery
articles.summary: D3-Gym is a newly introduced dataset designed to enhance data-driven discovery in scientific research by providing verifiable environments for 565 tasks derived from 239 real scientific repositories. This initiative aims to address the limitations of current language models and agents by offering a structured framework for testing and advancing their capabilities in real-world scientific contexts.

articles.title: Exploring the System 1 Thinking Capability of Large Reasoning Models
articles.summary: The paper examines the system 1 thinking capability of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), focusing on their intuitive response efficiency with minimal token usage. It highlights the need for further exploration of this ability, which is crucial for enhancing reasoning efficiency and difficulty awareness in real-world applications.
